newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA submits non-binding Axiom bid.
newsitem.headline: CBA submits non-binding Axiom bid.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia managing director David Murray said on Thursday the bank had submitted a non-binding bid to buy Axiom Funds Management from the New South Wales state government.
"We're interested in Axiom and we've submitted a non-binding bid required in the first round," he told reporters after an address to the Securities Institute.
Axiom, formerly known as State Super, has about A$17 billion of funds under management and manages the state's public sector retirement funds.
New South Wales Treasurer Michael Egan said last year the sale was expected to be completed in early 1997.
Local media reports have said Axiom has attracted indicative bids from about a dozen parties, including AMP Investments and ING Groep NV unit Mercantile Mutual.
A short-list of six bidders is expected to be prepared, with due diligence starting early in March.
